question: Name the function that walked the chunk list and tagged the two length fields from pc=0x3dff8c / ra=0x3dff90, and say what it does AFTER tagging.

walker.why_ra_is_pc_plus_4: the store is in the DELAY SLOT of the jal at 0x3dff88, so $ra = 0x3dff90 is that jal's return address, not a caller frame. The generated file carries `case 0x3dff90u: goto label_3dff90;` at line 26, which is the same return address.
walker.s1: the chunk TOTAL length, loaded at 0x3e006c `lw $s1, 0x4($s2)`
walker.s2: the CURRENT CHUNK HEADER pointer, loaded at 0x3e0058 `lw $s2, 0x54($s0)` -- i.e. the walk cursor lives at ctx0+0x54
walker.s5: the return of func_3DFE88, the chunk-KIND lookup

pseudocode: if ((magic & tbl[i].mask) == tbl[i].match) return tbl[i].kind  (0x3dfeb8 lw $v0, 0x8($a0))
classifier.meaning: the top byte is the registered chunk KIND from a {mask,match,kind} table, not a free-running visited counter

what_the_top_byte_means.read_by_producer: sub_003DFED0 at 0x3e0074 `and $v0, $s1, 0xFF000000`: a chunk whose length field still carries a nonzero top byte is treated as STILL QUEUED, and the walker overwrites it with an 8-byte sentinel stub (0x3e0084 len=8, 0x3e008c magic=$s6->[0x11c]) and then STOPS (0x3e0044: magic == sentinel -> return 1)
what_the_top_byte_means.read_by_consumer: sub_003E12E0 at 0x3e132c `and $s1, $v1, 0x00FFFFFF` then 0x3e1330 `sw $s1, 0x4($s2)`: the dequeue STRIPS the kind byte and writes the plain size back
what_the_top_byte_means.verdict: the top byte is an OCCUPANCY bit carrying the kind: set when the walker publishes the chunk, cleared when the consumer dequeues it. It is the producer/consumer handshake of a single-buffer ring, stored in the chunk header itself.

what_it_does_after_tagging: 0x3dff88  jal func_3E5700($s0+4)          -- take the stream lock (the tag store IS its delay slot)
0x3dffa4  slot = ctx0->[0x24] + ($s5<<4) - 0x10   -- the PER-KIND queue slot, 16 bytes
0x3dffb4  slot->[8] += $s1                -- publish: add this chunk to the kind byte count
0x3dffc4  if (slot->[8] == $s1) slot->[0xC] = $s2  -- first entry: set the head
0x3dffe8  ctx0->[0x54] += $s1             -- ADVANCE THE CURSOR past this chunk
0x3dfff4  if it crossed ctx0->[0x44] clear ctx0->[0x48]
0x3e0040  loop back to 0x3e0058 unless magic == sentinel
loop_exits: fewer than 8 bytes between cursor and ctx0->[0x58] (0x3e0064) -> return 0
chunk body not fully resident: ctx0->[0x58] < cursor + len (0x3e00a0) -> return 0

who_calls_the_walker.what_it_is: the READ-COMPLETION path: it adds the delivered byte count to ctx0->[0x170] (0x3e01e8) and to ctx0->[0x58] (the data end, 0x3e01f0) and only then runs the walker
who_calls_the_walker.consequence: the walker is driven by DATA ARRIVAL, never by consumption. Nothing on the consume path re-enters it.

where_the_tagged_chunk_goes: sub_003DFED0  publishes it into the per-kind slot at ctx0->[0x24] + (kind-1)*16
sub_003E12E0  dequeues the head (slot->[0xC]), STRIPS the kind byte, decrements slot->[8], and walks forward to the next chunk whose tag matches slot->[4] (the kind)
sub_003AEAD0  wraps the dequeued chunk in a 3-word descriptor {+0 header, +4 payload = header+8, +8 total length} and stages it in the source object's one-slot pushback at 0x5487c0
sub_003B0B40  memcpy(dst=self->[0x7C], src=desc->[4], n=desc->[8]-8), zero-pads to ((total+7) & ~0xF), then sceMpegAddBs(mpeg, dst, that size)

the_5040_derived_statically.pad: the loop at 0x3b0bb8-0x3b0bd0 zero-fills from offset 5028 up to $s2 + 0x10; the first 12 of those zeros are inside the 5040 that is fed
the_5040_derived_statically.agrees_with: E24 and E26 measured 5028 ES + 12 zero pad = 5040 from the bytes; the source produces exactly that arithmetic
